condition: subacute bloody diarrhea 5 times daily with abdominal cramps and 6 kg weight loss over 8 weeks
level_rationale: Eight weeks of abdominal cramping, 6 kg unintentional weight loss, and passing loose bloody stools 5 times daily in a 24-year-old strongly indicates inflammatory bowel disease requiring gastroenterology specialist evaluation and ileocolonoscopy, whereas passing large maroon blood clots into the toilet 4 times within 1 hour indicates brisk acute lower gastrointestinal hemorrhage requiring immediate emergency department resuscitation and hemostatic intervention.

attribution.source: Cross E, Prior JA, Farmer AD, Saunders B (2023). Patients' views and experiences of delayed diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease: a qualitative study. BJGP Open.
attribution.title: Patients' views and experiences of delayed diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease: a qualitative study.
attribution.location: Results — Normalising symptoms, quote (F, aged 45 years, CD)
attribution.evidence: I did put it down to just like stress at work, you know, [inspection at work] and stuff like that, I assumed because I’d never been ill, I’d hardly ever been ill before … I thought I’d just go back to how I was and I think maybe there is a bit of burying your head in the sand sometimes as well, you know, maybe knowing things aren’t quite right but hoping they’d just sort themselves out on their own.
attribution.adaptation: Adapted verbatim Crohn's disease patient causal normalization 'put it down to just like stress at work' into present-tense belief clause 'and I think it's stress at work'.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain young-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + sourced work-stress causal normalization belief clause (-att, Cross 2023) + single-fact lower GI hemorrhage escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic reference facts (age 24, 8 weeks of abdominal cramps, 6 kg weight loss, and 5 loose bloody stools daily) without naming Crohn's or colitis, with an exact 18-vs-18 word span swap and zero stated negatives. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, escalating only bowel bleeding output in f4 from 5 loose bloody stools daily to passing large maroon blood clots into the toilet 4 times this hour keeps the 8-week GI case completely coherent while shifting care cleanly from gastroenterology specialist evaluation (level 3) to emergency department hemorrhage resuscitation (level 4).
